title: Three ways of saying “we’re not your dad’s RadioShack”
lede: For most of its life the pitch was service: “You’ve got questions. We’ve got answers.” Later campaigns tried to escape the image of a dusty parts store, and spent less money each time.

rows: The store clerk as expert. The trademark was still among the assets sold in 2020[^28]
Store-within-a-store alliances shown on the home page[^33]
Wireless kept growing, computers did not (no sales split in our sources)
An advertising nickname to modernize the image. Signs and the legal name stayed RadioShack[^23][^36]
Advertising spend fell to $193.0M that year[^11]

blocks.title: “The Shack,” 2009
blocks.body: In August 2009 the company began calling itself “The Shack” in advertising while the store signs stayed the same.[^23][^36] Ad spending that year fell to $193.0M, the lowest since 1999 at the time (derived from the 10-K series above).
